thread.title: Big Tech shake-up — three stocks to buy and three to sell - MarketWatch

author: Jeff Reeves
title: Big Tech shake-up — three stocks to buy and three to sell - MarketWatch
text:
A big story in the past few years has been the dominance of Big Tech, and for good reason.
In calendar 2017, the FAANG stocks — Facebook FB, +0.89% Apple AAPL, +1.98% Amazon AMZN, +1.46% Netflix NFLX, +2.88% and Google owner Alphabet GOOG, +1.51% GOOGL, +1.38% — were up between 31% and 54% to trounce even the impressive 21% gain for the S&P 500 SPX, +1.18% in the same period.
Furthermore, these mega-sized technology companies make up an increasing share of investor portfolios regardless of whether they buy individual stocks. Thanks to the weighting of the S&P 500 by market value, Apple represents just shy of 4% of the entire index right now, and in the more focused Nasdaq 100, the tech giant represents a massive 11%.
If you’re tired of the focus on big tech companies, I don’t blame you. But the reality is that a responsible investor simply cannot ignore this sector, particularly in 2018, as many of the big tech names seem to be diverging after a very important earnings season.
Here’s the state of play in Big Tech, with three companies that look to be building on their 2017 success … and three more that seem to be falling behind in this fast-moving sector.

Tech stock to buy: Microsoft
While there are certainly sexier names in tech, Microsoft Corp. MSFT, +1.45% has been quietly building a case over the past two years that it is one of the best large-cap tech stocks out there.
For starters, it boasts the same scale as some of the more fashionable names. With a market cap of over $700 billion, it is neck and neck with Amazon and Alphabet. Furthermore, a cash hoard valued at over $140 billion makes it second only to Apple in its war chest. That’s all on top of a jaw-dropping $40 billion in annual operating cash flow.
But don’t just think MSFT is resting on these attributes to win over investors. Its evolution as a cloud computing and software-as-a-service giant is proving very successful, as evidenced by great earnings a few weeks ago that featured an amazing 98% surge in its Azure arm and a 41% jump in Office 365.
Many tech companies boast a great balance sheet and impressive scale. However, MSFT also is showing great growth metrics in the parts of its business that matter most to its future success.
That’s a winning combination for any tech company, even one belonging to the old guard like Microsoft.
Tech stock to buy: Cisco
Speaking of fuddy-duddy tech stocks, Cisco Systems CSCO, +3.09% is also worth a look from investors despite a rather lackluster reputation in some corners of the market.
But much to the pleasure of shareholders, Cisco is finally making some big strides in restructuring its legacy business. Recurring revenue from software is replacing hardware sales, and CSCO has been so successful in this effort lately that it posted its first quarterly revenue increase in more than two years .
More to the point, shares finally eclipsed their pre-recession peak at the end of 2017 to hit the highest level since the dot-com days. And in 2018, shares have surged 13% since Jan. 1. The company also raised its dividend 14% to 33 cents a share, a more than five-fold increase since instituting the payout back in 2011, and raised its buyback program to $25 billion.
The growth in software subscriptions isn’t just fueling these headlines now. Thanks to the nature of its licensing and annual fees, that revenue will continue to be recorded going forward and provide a strong foundation for future growth.
It’s much the same as the story of Microsoft. And however much you’d prefer to buy a fashionable tech stock over a stodgy old-school name, you shouldn’t overlook the impressive performance and big potential of CSCO.
Tech stock to buy: Amazon
Of course, some of the FAANG stocks are widely held for very good reason, as is the case with Amazon.
There are many reasons to own this tech titan. But the two biggest reasons I’m bullish include its Prime subscription service and the potential for grocery sales after the Whole Foods acquisition.
With Prime, the company has begun reporting partial information to investors via a Subscription Services segment. There’s no detailed view of total subscribers but total revenue booked from subscription products ballooned to $9.7 billion in fiscal 2017, up 51% from the prior year. That’s a tremendous baseline of revenue but also a springboard to even bigger sales; one report late last year said the average annual sales of a Prime customer is roughly $1,300 annually — nearly double a conventional Amazon shopper’s average spend.
As for grocery sales, Amazon already has the know-how to take its e-commerce expertise into the field and dominate going forward. But many investors may not know AMZN is already an industry leader in the fresh-foods space without some ambitious effort to disrupt things. According to a study by One Click Retail, the e-commerce giant owns about 18% of online grocery sales to tally $2 billion in current sales.
It may seem hyperbole to say the sky is the limit for Amazon, but you can’t count this company out of any category. But with shares up 27% so far this year, even as other tech stocks have stumbled, AMZN certainly seems to be living up to all the hype.
Tech stock to sell: Facebook
Investors are used to Facebook topping their expectations each earnings season, and got another dose of that at the end of January with another big beat . However, the deeper details show that all is not exactly well at the social-media king.
For starters, its daily active users in the U.S. and Canada — its most lucrative market — declined for the first time in its history as a publicly traded company. FB is clearly hitting maturity, but even more disturbing are active management decisions to limit engagement. That includes a tweak to the algorithm that reduced appearances of viral videos and caused the typical user to spend about 5% less time on the site. Plans to staff up an additional 10,000 or so cybersecurity staffers will also add a significant expense burden.
Bigger picture, Facebook also faces an existential threat as the idea that using social media frequently may be bad for your mental health . That’s to say nothing of bad actors spreading misinformation on the platform, be it Russia interfering in the 2016 election or the reprehensible stories lately that falsely claim aggrieved students from the Florida school shooting are actually just paid actors.
With this kind of brand tarnish and slowing momentum in key operating metrics, it may be time to book your gains in Facebook and look elsewhere if you’re a shareholder. FB stock is off about 7% from highs just a few weeks ago, and that may be a sign of things to come.
Tech stock to sell: Alphabet
While Facebook at least managed to put up strong earnings for the prior quarter, Google operator Alphabet faces some of the same big-picture risks but also managed to disappoint analysts in its recent earnings .
Details showed a huge increase in traffic-acquisition costs — a big challenge that doesn’t seem to be going away. Thanks in part to these charges and other margin-pinching expenses, adjusted profits widely missed the mark.
While its high-profile bets on things like self-driving cars and cloud computing are captivating, the sad reality is that online advertising is still the biggest driver of Google. This business accounted for more than 86% of total revenue in fiscal 2017 and pressure on margins here matters much more than anything else.
To make matters worse, the once-dominant perch Google held in the online advertising space is being challenged. That includes the emerging threat of mobile and app-based search alternatives, as well as more overt efforts like European Union antitrust fines last year that were a record $2.8 billion .
If your dominance is threatened even as your current scale isn’t cutting it with investors, that’s not a good place to be. A deep plunge of about 15% immediately after earnings shows that Wall Street may have GOOG stock on a very short leash right now.
Tech stock to sell: Nvidia
High-flier Nvidia NVDA, +0.26% won over plenty of investors last year as its shares doubled and its graphics cards were the go-to choice for cryptocurrency miners around the world. But as bitcoin and cryptocurrency struggles with wild volatility and as NVDA stock now trades for a forward P/E of about 34 after the run-up, it may be time to cool it and look for other alternatives in the sector.
The most tangible reason for shopping around came just a few weeks ago as Nvidia stock plunged about 15% in just four trading days across early February. And while it did set a new all-time high around $250 in January, it has tested but failed to break through that resistance on several occasions.
Yes, shares have made back the worst part of February losses. And, yes, NVDA is still up an impressive 25% this year, with more than 20% sales growth projected this year. However, the risk of a waning crypto market along with slower growth rates raise the stakes and create plenty of opportunity for downside volatility.
That’s not to say that Nvidia will crash and burn in 2018, but just that investors have plenty of better alternatives right now, particularly as the market seems to be getting more discerning about large-cap tech stocks.
